observerCard.title: Three Reads: which tank is |x+2|?
observerCard.frame: The second tank is g(x) = ___ because the ___ (input / output) changed by ___, which moves the graph ___.
observerCard.body:
## Setup
Tank 1 drains for 5 h, is empty at x = 0, refills for 4 h: f(x) = |x| on [-5, 4]. Tank 2 started 2 hours earlier. Which translation? A |x|+2, B |x+2|, C |x|-2, D |x-2|. Sheet: a2_1-2_three_reads.pdf.

## Read 1 (2 min)
Read aloud. Pairs: what is the situation, no numbers. One pair reports.

## Read 2 (3 min)
What do x, y and x = 0 mean? Whiteboards: write what x = 0 means for tank 1.

## Read 3 (2 min)
What is the question asking? Pairs restate it in their own words.

## Decide (3 min)
Whiteboards: when is tank 2 empty? Input or output? Which way does the graph move? Answer B, |x+2|. Watch for D (sign trap: earlier feels like minus) and A or C (gallons instead of time).

## Exit
Say the frame aloud with a partner, then write it.

observerCard.frame: 2f(x - 1) means the output is ___ (doubled) and the graph moves ___ by ___, so the point (a, b) lands at ___.
observerCard.body:
## Setup
SAT day, 40 minutes. Two IXL Web Jams, same as the other sections, then the short 1-2 quiz (Savvas items 1, 3, 5).

## Web Jam NNY (7 min)
Dilations. Students answer on their own devices; the class score shows on the board. After each item: whiteboards, is it the input or the output that was stretched? Watch for 2f(x) read as a horizontal stretch.

## Web Jam RSN (8 min)
Combined transformations. Whiteboards: draw a 2f(x - 1)-style graph by hand from a given f before checking the Jam answer. Say the frame aloud with a partner.

## Quiz (remaining time)
1-2 Lesson Quiz, short form. Items 2 and 3 count 10 each, item 1 is a 5-point bonus. Quiet, individual.

## Exit
Quiz collected. Under 20 may replace the score with IXL SmartScore 70 on NNY, RSN, KQL.

## Preparing (3 min)
Hand out the 1-3 packet (a2_1-3_fast.pdf). Example 3 page of the PDF shown on the SMART board (no iPad pen today): freeze the board and write on the frozen page with the board's tray pen; unfreeze to turn the page, freeze again. Pairs: how many pieces, and where does each start and stop? Name the open point at (1, -1) and the closed point at (1, 4). Students mark both points on their packet copy.

## Interacting (7 min)
Whiteboards, one step per round, boards up each round, one board explains with the frame while the teacher writes that step on the frozen board. Round 1: the interval for piece A (-2 <= x < 1). Round 2: slope from two points (3). Round 3: use (-2, -10) to find b (-4), so 3x - 4. Pairs then do piece B the same way (x + 3 on 1 <= x <= 5), then piece C (slope 0, so 8), writing each rule into the packet as it is confirmed.

## Extending (2 min)
One student comes to the SMART board and assembles the three rules into case notation under the graph; the class copies it into the packet. Ask: why x < 1 for A and 1 <= x for B? Each x gets exactly one piece.

## Fallback
Board not cooperating: draw the three pieces by hand on the whiteboard side of the room; everything else stays the same. Short on time: piece A only on whiteboards, then everyone says the frame.

observerCard.title: Three Reads + think-pair-share: the shipping step function
observerCard.frame: On the interval ___ the cost is ___, so the piece is a horizontal segment, open at ___ and closed at ___.
observerCard.body:
## Three Reads of the table (3 min, no pens)
Shipping table on the board (Example 5, a2_1-3_fast.pdf): 0 < x <= 2 costs 5, 2 < x <= 4 costs 8, 4 < x <= 6 costs 11, 6 < x <= 8 costs 14. Read 1: what is the situation? Read 2: what are x and y, and what does one row say in words (more than 2 lb, up to and including 4, costs 8)? Read 3: what are we asked to do?

## Think-pair-share on whiteboards (6 min)
Axes first (weight 0 to 8, cost 0 to 16). Then one row per round. Think: plot the one step alone. Pair: compare boards, agree which end is open (left open, right closed: exactly 2 lb costs 5, not 8). Share: boards up, one student says the frame for that step. Give round 2 the most time.

## Extend (2 min)
Name the shape: a step function, all horizontal pieces. Boards: domain {x | 0 < x <= 8}, range {5, 8, 11, 14}, minimum 5, maximum 14. Ask: why is 0 not in the domain?

## Then
Try It 5 (parking lot table) in pairs on the packet, then Web Jam RVD.
